newsitem.title: UK: UK's Oftel details phone network charge plan.
newsitem.headline: UK's Oftel details phone network charge plan.

text.p: Industry regulator OFTEL on Tuesday detailed its plans for British Telecommunications Plc network charges.
The watchdog suggests a 6 to 12 percent range for X in the RPI-X formula to control the baskets of non-competetive and bottleneck services.
The services in the controlled baskets represent about one billion stg out of BT's total costs of 12 billion stg, OFTEL said.
Safeguard capsd account for a further 0.4 billion stg.
The proposed controls would run from October 1, 1997 to September 30, 2001.

"Overall the proposals give BT more flexibility to set charges and mark a reduction in detailed and intrusive regulation," OFTEL said, adding that charges for all interconnection services would fall under its proposals.
The regulator said charges for non-competitive services, such as call-termination, would fall by 22 to 40 percent in real terms by 2001 under its charge control plan.
The consultation period for the proposals runs to June 10 witha further two weeks for comments on responses received.
